note:
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found incidentally on chest imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a patient with a 3-month history of intermittent cough that began after loading hay while working with horses. Patient subsequently developed a cold and presented to their PCP. PCP diagnosed bronchitis and obtained a chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia, which revealed a lung nodule. CT scan confirmed the nodule, and patient was referred for evaluation. Patient notes that cough has since resolved. Patient reports regular exercise including biking and does not typically get sick. Patient expresses anxiety about the nodule finding.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies pain, shortness of breath, or other symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
No family history of lung cancer. Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. No previous family history of lung infections or pneumonia.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active individual who exercises regularly with biking. Former smoker who quit approximately 7 years ago. Has horses. Reports being encouraged to quit smoking by children and feels better since cessation.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure 124/76, heart rate 70, respiratory rate 16, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart regular rate and rhythm with no clicks, rubs, murmurs, or extra beats. Skin pink, warm, and dry. No edema in lower extremities. Small swelling noted on knuckles of third digits bilaterally, consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities. Capillary refill brisk.

RESULTS
Chest CT showing a solitary 2 cm nodule in the lateral aspect of the right upper lobe with smooth appearance. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule. Will order pulmonary function tests for baseline assessment of lung function. Will schedule PET CT to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Recommended video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) for removal of nodule with small portion of lung via three small incisions on right chest under general anesthesia, procedure duration approximately 1.5 hours. Post-operative chest tube to remain in place until the following day, removed at bedside. Hospital admission anticipated for one night with discharge the next day. Nodule could be benign but removal recommended given patient's smoking history. Patient to continue follow-up with rheumatologist and continue current rheumatoid arthritis medication therapy as previously outlined.
